  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE

Tuesday, June 16, 2020  6:00 PM  Teleconference

Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, General Plan Advisory Committee Members will be
participating via teleconference.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
848 1898 5336, Password: 515335. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 848 1898 5336, Password: 515335.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JUNE 16, 2020

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Addleman,  Arata, Carman,  Carrese,
  Corman,  Seamans,  Shinn,  Stegura,
  Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bayer, Buresh, Medawar, Schmitz, Silvano,
  Stegura

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  Aaron Lobliner, Planner, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Land Use Planner, Michael Baker International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  MAY 20, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
CORMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MAY 20, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  LAND USE ELEMENT

John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International (MBI), stated that the meeting tonight will focus
on land use matters that do not involve the commercial district. Mr. Bellas introduced Dan Wery,
who presented the Land Use Element.

Dan Wery, Land Use Planner, Michael Baker International, provided an overview on the purpose
of the Land Use Element, including:
  • 20 to 30 Vision, Goals, Guidance – Long view
  • Land Use – Location, Nature, Character, Intensity, Balance
  • Factors and Obligations
  o Changes in population – Younger families moving in and think of long term.
  o Markets and economics – Change in retail space due to online options.
  o Affordable housing obligations – Finding available sites to meet housing
  obligations.
  o Mobility options

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 DRAFT MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2020
   o  Limited land and redevelopment opportunities – There is limited available space,
  so redevelopment may need to be explored.

Mr. Wery stated that the Land Use Element is a key element of the general plan. It affects all other
elements, including: Housing Element, Circulation Element, Open Space and Recreation Element
and Conservation Element.

Mr. Wery stated that the discussion will focus on the areas that are subject to change in the next
20 to 30 years. Stable residential areas and established open space, recreation, public facilities
and utilities will be excluded.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN inquired about the park that is being developed on the north
east corner of Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN)/Palos Verdes Drive East (PVDE) and asked how
it will be addressed on the land use maps.

Director Wahba asked MBI to make a note of this since it should redesignated and zoned as Open
Space.

Discussion Site 1 – North side of Hawthorne Blvd. (between Silver Spur Rd. and PVDN)
  • Currently vacant
  • Zoned RA-15
  • GPLU – Medium density residential
  • Planning Area 4
  • Options for site:
  o Multi-family residential
  o Open space/parks
  o Neighborhood Commercial

Mr. Wery stated that some of the constraints for the site are the steep slopes and direct access.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN asked about the access. Mr. Wery stated that one option
would be for a home be removed from the top or a land reduction on Hawthorne Blvd.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the road couldn’t be narrowed due to high traffic and there would
be issues with the neighboring city. He also stated that is is not well suited for commercial.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Planning Manager Naughton confirmed that
the parcel is city-owned. Director Wahba stated from the last General Plan Update, this parcel
was going to be preserved as open space and noted that the public right-of-way below this site
belongs to Rancho Palos Verdes.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS agreed that this should remain as open space.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that this parcel should be kept as a potential option to
meeting housing demand and stated that after all areas are discussed a decision can be made
on the best use for all of the sites.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN agreed that this parcel should be kept as a housing option.

Discussion Site 2 - Dapplegray Elementary School
  • Currently elementary school
  • Zoned Institutional
  • GPLU Institutional
  • Planning Area 2
  • Options for site:
  o Expanded school
  o Affordable teacher housing
  o Open space/parks
  o Single Family (SF) Residential

Mr. Wery stated that some schools are building affordable housing for teachers. If housing was
developed and made affordable; this would meet some of the city’s affordable housing obligations.
When looking at the site, there is a lot of excess area and an area adjacent to the school that is
landlocked but has the potential of having access.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 DRAFT MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2020
 Examples of schools and school districts that have done this were provided, one of which includes
Chadwick School.

A discussion ensued.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that this is a fantastic idea and stated that this school
used to be a middle school and has more acreage than what would be required for an elementary
school.

Discussion Site 3 – Palos Verdes Peninsula High School
  • Currently High School
  • Zoned Institutional
  • GPLU Institutional
  • Planning Area 6
  • Options for site:
  o Affordable teacher housing.

Mr. Wery stated that this could also be an option for affordable housing for teachers/staff,
however, this would be more constrained and there are a lot of slopes on the north east side.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked if a special designation could be created for workforce housing at
school sites. Mr. Wery stated that a policy could be built in to the general plan and if necessary,
amend the zoning.

Discussion Site 4 – Equestrian Center
  • Currently Open Space, Horse Trail, Equestrian center
  • Zoned Agricultural
  • GPLU Commercial Recreation
  • Planning Area 3
  • Options for site:
  o Revise zoning from A- Agricultural to CR – Commercial Recreation

There was no discussion on this site.

Discussion Site 5 – General Store and Daycare (Kelly’s Corner)
  • Currently Commercial and Day Care
  • Zoning – RA-20
  • GPLU – Neighborhood Commercial
  • Planning Area 5
  • Options for site:
  o Rezone from RA-20 to CL – Commercial Limited
  o Expanded Commercial and/or Mixed Use
  o Multi-family Residential

Mr. Wery stated that there is a lot of excess space at this site and has the potential to get greater
use.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Wery stated that this is in the Landmark
Overlay.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that this is the last historical site in the city and was the original City
Hall.

Surabhi Barbhaya, MBI, stated that the idea is to keep Kelly’s corner and develop behind it.

Director Wahba stated that is would be difficult to build a multi-family residential behind it and
keep the integrity of how the site was developed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN commented that looking at the history and how it is
connected to the city, he recommends that it is left as it is.

A brief discussion ensued on the type of development that should be recommended at the site.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 DRAFT MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2020
 John Bellas, MBI confirmed that the committee consensus is that the frontage of the corner should
be left as is; beyond that, if there is an opportunity for a low-scale development in the rear north
west of the property.

Discussion Site 5 – General Store and Daycare (Kelly’s Corner)
  • Currently Commercial and Day Care
  • Zoning – RA-20
  • GPLU – Neighborhood Commercial
  • Planning Area 5
  • Options for site:
  o Rezone from RA-20 to CL – Commercial Limited
  o Expanded Commercial and/or Mixed Use
  o Multi-family Residential
  o
Discussion Site 6 – Academy Center Office Buildings
  • Currently Office Buildings
  • Zoning – Commercial Office
  • GPLU – Commercial Office
  • Planning Area 3
  • Options for site:
  o Keep CO-Commercial Office
  o Encourage more intensive development
  o Mixed Use
  o Multi-family Residential

Mr. Wery stated that as these buildings age out, other uses may be developed.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN expressed concern with traffic in that intersection. Director Wahba stated
that this could be looked at when reviewing the Transportation Element.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN stated that this should be kept as commercial office and
would not recommend residential use.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE stated that these buildings should be rebuilt and stated that
there is a need for office space.

Discussion Site 7 – Sea Horse Riding Club
  • Currently Riding Club
  • Zoning – Commercial Recreation
  • GPLU – Commercial Recreation
  • Planning Area 3
  • Options for site:
  o Open Space/Parks
  o Commercial Recreation
  o Multi-family Residential
  o Expanded RHE City Hall Complex

Mr. Wery stated that this site has a lot of open space. There is potential to develop something
that compliments the City Hall site.

Director Wahba stated that the owner of this site has approached him regarding changing the use
to something other than equestrian.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN stated that she is not in favor of changing the zoning of this site
in order to encourage keeping the horses in a private facility. She stated that Sea Horse is just as
much of an icon as Kelly’s Corner.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS agreed and stated that we have to be careful in eliminating
equestrian facilities.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN agreed to leave it as-is.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Director Wahba stated that this site is
approximately four acres.
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  4
 DRAFT MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested a community gathering space.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN agreed that it should be kept as equestrian for now.

Mr. Bellas confirmed that the consensus is that it should not be designated for residential or
commercial use. The site should stay commercial recreation but there may be a policy for future
acquisition by the city for future use as a community gathering space.

Discussion Site 8 – Vacant Corner at Crest and Highridge

Director Wahba stated that this site is under construction and should be removed from the list.

No further discussion on this site.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN inquired about the site on Highridge past Armaga Springs that is
Condominium Office and if this could be an opportunity site. Director Wahba stated that the units
are individually owned.

A brief discussion ensued on the feasibility of developing this site.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Director Wahba stated that ADU’s could be
counted towards meeting the city’s housing obligations. Planning Manager Naughton further
explained how the ADU’s could be reported towards meeting Regional Housing Needs Allocation
(RHNA) numbers.

Discussion Site 9 – Hawthorne at Crest Residential
  • Currently Single Family Residential
  • Zoning - Commercial Limited
  • GPLU – Neighborhood Commercial
  • Planning Area 7 1:24:50
  • Options for site:
  o Commercial Limited
  o Medium Density Residential

Director Wahba provided a brief history on this site.

The committee agreed to remove this site from the opportunity sites list.

Mr. Wery thanked the committee for the discussion and if there are are further questions or
comments, please forward them to staff.

The next meeting will focus on the Commercial District opportunities.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN requested that the scenic corridor be discussed at a future meeting.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE inquired if information on geological/water issues in the
commercial district can be provided. Mr. Wery responded that they are aware of the issues and
will take them into consideration when making recommendations.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that in addition to the zoning map, there are distinct planning areas
with their own guidelines and asked if they will this be continued or revised. Mr. Wery stated that
there is a plan to put this on a future agenda for discussion.

6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF/COMMITTEE ITEMS
NONE

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 7:58 p.m.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved by,

_________________________________  ___________________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Steve Zuckerman, Chair

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
